root_cause.text: In fanotify’s fsnotify_prepare_user_wait() mark iteration, a failure from fsnotify_get_mark_safe() was treated as fatal without checking whether the detached fsnotify_mark belonged to the current notification group, so a stale mark from an unrelated group could incorrectly abort permission-event handling and bypass the permission check.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “fsnotify_get_mark_safe() may return false for a mark on an unrelated group, which results in bypassing the permission check,” and the patch changes fsnotify_prepare_user_wait() to loop past detached marks whose mark->group != iter_info->current_group using fsnotify_next_mark(), only failing when the removed mark is in the current group.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states “fsnotify_get_mark_safe() may return false for a mark on an unrelated group, which results in bypassing the permission check,” and the patch changes fsnotify_prepare_user_wait() to loop past detached marks whose mark->group != iter_info->current_group using fsnotify_next_mark(), only failing when the removed mark is in the current group.

intent_record.intent_summary: Export fsnotify_next_mark from file-local scope so it can be used outside its current source file.
intent_record.what: The function definition of fsnotify_next_mark was changed by removing the static storage-class specifier, making it a non-static function while leaving its signature and body otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: This change gives fsnotify_next_mark external linkage so it can be referenced from other translation units, without altering its internal runtime logic or behavior when called.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop fsnotify_get_mark_safe() from silently succeeding on NULL input so it only operates on valid mark objects.
intent_record.what: The change removes the initial null-pointer check from fsnotify_get_mark_safe() that previously returned true when mark was NULL, leaving the function to immediately operate on mark->refcnt and mark->lock.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer treats a NULL mark pointer as a successful case and instead assumes callers pass a valid non-NULL mark, preventing NULL from being silently accepted and enforcing the function's expectation of a real mark object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip removed marks from unrelated groups during fsnotify user-wait preparation so only current-group mark removal causes failure.
intent_record.what: The code now introduces a local `mark` variable initialized from `iter_info->marks[type]` inside the iterator loop, replaces a single `fsnotify_get_mark_safe(iter_info->marks[type])` check with a `while (mark && !fsnotify_get_mark_safe(mark))` loop, adds a conditional that fails only when the unpinnable mark belongs to `iter_info->current_group`, otherwise advances to `fsnotify_next_mark(mark)` and updates `iter_info->marks[type]`, and updates the comment from referring to "both marks" in "inode / vfsmount" lists to "all marks" in "inode / vfsmount / etc" lists.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer immediately fails when the current mark cannot be safely referenced if that mark belongs to some unrelated group being removed. Instead, it skips such unrelated stale marks, advances the iterator to the next mark, and only aborts when the unreferenceable mark is from the current group being processed. This allows user wait preparation to continue correctly across multiple mark lists and avoids unnecessary failure caused by concurrently removed marks from other groups.

intent_record.intent_summary: Export the `fsnotify_next_mark` prototype in the header so other code can iterate fsnotify marks using this helper.
intent_record.what: A new function declaration was added to the header: `struct fsnotify_mark *fsnotify_next_mark(struct fsnotify_mark *mark);` alongside the existing fsnotify mark management extern declarations.
intent_record.how: This exposes the `fsnotify_next_mark` symbol to other compilation units, allowing external code to call the function to obtain the next `fsnotify_mark` in whatever traversal or iteration logic it implements; previously, such code could not legally reference this function through the header interface.

grouping_result.intent: Export the `fsnotify_next_mark` prototype in the header so other code can iterate fsnotify marks using this helper.
Stop fsnotify_get_mark_safe() from silently succeeding on NULL input so it only operates on valid mark objects.
Skip removed marks from unrelated groups during fsnotify user-wait preparation so only current-group mark removal causes failure.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make fsnotify_next_mark available outside its original source file by changing its linkage and declaring it in the public header.

relevance_review.reason: This group only changes symbol visibility for fsnotify_next_mark by exporting it and adding a header declaration. It does not address the permission-event logic, fsnotify_get_mark_safe() failure handling, or checking whether a detached mark belongs to the current notification group.

The root cause is incorrect handling of fsnotify_get_mark_safe() failures during fanotify mark iteration, specifically not verifying whether a detached mark belonged to the current group before aborting permission handling. This change only prevents silent success on NULL input and does not address the group-membership check or the improper fatal handling of unrelated stale marks.

The change directly matches the root cause: it alters fsnotify user-wait/mark iteration logic to ignore removed or stale marks from unrelated groups, preventing an unrelated detached mark from aborting permission-event handling.

candidates.rationale: This conditional treats any failure to pin a mark as a fatal error. Per the root cause, it fails to distinguish whether the detached mark belongs to the current notification group, so an unrelated stale mark can incorrectly abort permission-event handling.

This unconditional failure path is the mechanism by which a failed fsnotify_get_mark_safe() aborts processing. Without checking that the removed mark is from the current group, it enables unrelated detached marks to bypass the permission check.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition treats any failure to safely pin the iterated mark as fatal. The root cause is that it does not verify whether the detached mark belongs to the current notification group, so a stale removed mark from an unrelated group can trigger the failure path and incorrectly abort permission-event handling.

This is the fatal abort taken after fsnotify_get_mark_safe() fails. Because the preceding check does not distinguish unrelated detached marks from current-group marks, this statement causes processing to fail and can bypass the intended permission check.
